clue.text: Character found in Chinese literature

parts.note: Chinese writing uses symbols standing for whole ideas rather than sounds, so a character in that script is the thing described

explanation.surface: A reader spots a figure appearing in a Chinese novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' tempts you towards a person in a story; here it is a written symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A written symbol that represents an idea or thing directly, as Chinese script does, is this kind of sign.

clue.text: Fish from bow or stern of dinghy

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a boat, so it points to the front letter of the word dinghy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a boat, so it points to the final letter of the word dinghy

explanation.surface: An angler pulls a fish over the front or back of a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow or stern' reads as a choice; in fact you take D (the bow of dinghy), the word OR, then Y (its stern).
explanation.definitionFit: The John Dory is an edible sea fish, often just called by its short name.

clue.text: Seed part of field before usual time for sowing

indicators.note: one piece is placed ahead of the other in this down answer

parts.note: in cricket the off side is one half of the field
spring is the season when most seeds are sown

explanation.surface: A farmer sows part of a field ahead of the normal season.
explanation.walkthrough: OFF is the cricket term for the side of the field the batsman faces; cricket is Britain's bat-and-ball summer game.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed in the old biblical sense means descendants, children or progeny.

clue.text: Dry fruit is naturally being watered?

indicators.note: something watered naturally is out in a shower, so the word is goes into the falling water

parts.note: nature's own watering comes as rain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dried fruit wonders whether it is getting a natural soaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: 'being watered' acts as the container signal, since nature's watering is a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is the classic dried fruit.

clue.text: What' might ensure time is ten to two, say

definitions.text: What' might ensure time is ten to two, say

parts.words: What' might ensure time is ten to two, say
parts.note: ten to two reads like a clock time, but here it is a jury split of ten jurors against two, which can still convict and so send a defendant to prison for some time

explanation.surface: Something guarantees that the clock shows 1.50.
explanation.walkthrough: In English courts a jury may convict by ten votes to two; 'time' is a prison sentence, not the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict reached when most but not all jurors agree, such as ten against two, can send someone to jail.

clue.text: Show outdated record in limited reference book

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a dictionary cut short gives dict
an EP, an extended-play disc, is an old record format

explanation.surface: Someone displays an old record inside a slim reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' means the reference book is cut off: DICT(ionary).
explanation.definitionFit: To portray or represent something in a picture or words is to show it.

clue.text: This servant could be foreign, however

definitions.text: This servant could be foreign, however

parts.words: This servant could be foreign, however
parts.note: a household servant may come from abroad, yet the word for one is also the opposite of foreign, as in home affairs versus overseas

explanation.surface: An employer notes that the household help might come from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the word's two senses: a home help, and 'home' as opposed to foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: A household worker such as a maid or cleaner is called by this word, which also means home-grown rather than overseas.

clue.text: Sort of book that has outstanding pictures

definitions.text: Sort of book that has outstanding pictures

parts.words: Sort of book that has outstanding pictures
parts.note: outstanding is read literally as standing out from the page, as in a children's book whose cut-out illustrations rise when opened

explanation.surface: A publisher praises a volume full of excellent illustrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise; it means the pictures physically stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's book whose paper figures rise up as each page opens is described this way.

clue.text: Unlike his wife, Jack wasn't prepared to chat like this

definitions.text: Unlike his wife, Jack wasn't prepared to chat like this

parts.words: Unlike his wife, Jack wasn't prepared to chat like this
parts.note: the nursery rhyme says Jack Sprat could eat no fat while his wife could eat no lean, so he would not chomp on fat, an idiom for talking

explanation.surface: A husband, unlike his spouse, refuses to make small talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat, from an English nursery rhyme, would eat no fat; his wife would eat no lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing the fat is an idiom for chatting idly at length.

clue.text: Improvise after trade gets into difficulty, in a way

indicators.note: this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: to traffic is to trade, often illicitly
musicians who jam improvise together

explanation.surface: A business has to busk it once trading gets into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' makes the definition a pun: a difficulty on a road, a way.
explanation.definitionFit: A road blockage of stationary vehicles is a difficulty literally found on a road.

clue.text: Expression of relief after power cut

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
to hew is to cut with blows

explanation.surface: Someone sighs with relief once the electricity goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power cut' reads as a blackout; it is P then HEW.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation people utter when an ordeal is over, or when it is very hot.

clue.text: Pleasurable route arranged to rim, perhaps

definitions.text: Pleasurable route arranged to rim, perhaps

parts.words: Pleasurable route arranged to rim, perhaps
parts.note: a garden walk might be edged with pale spring flowers set along its border, giving the phrase for an easy life of pleasure

explanation.surface: A garden walk is laid out with flowers lining its edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal picture is a path rimmed with spring flowers; the phrase means a life of pleasure that leads to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: From Shakespeare, a path of dalliance means an easy, pleasant course, usually ending in disaster.

clue.text: Dress, then depart for drive

parts.note: to get up is to dress, especially in a costume
and can mean then, as in 'wash and dry'
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: Someone gets dressed and then leaves for a car journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' looks like a car trip but is the noun meaning energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive as a noun means energy and initiative, enthusiasm for getting things done.

clue.text: Source of special fare from Eastern capital, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, standing for one spelt differently

parts.note: New Delhi is the capital of India, in the East

explanation.surface: Special food comes from a city in the East, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling special prepared foods.

clue.text: It may be considered unlucky when their net breaks

indicators.note: a net that breaks has its parts torn apart and reformed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fishermen think it bad luck when their net tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges THEIRNET.
explanation.definitionFit: The number after twelve is widely held to bring bad luck, as on Friday the 13th.

clue.text: Achieving good results with box cameras

definitions.text: Achieving good results with box cameras

parts.words: Achieving good results with box cameras
parts.note: box is slang for television, so the cameras are TV ones, and someone who looks good on them suits the screen

explanation.surface: A photographer gets fine pictures with simple old box cameras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is British slang for the television set; a box camera is a simple early camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who comes across well on television is said to have this quality.

clue.text: Tiny lines under foot

indicators.note: in a down answer this piece sits below the other

parts.note: a tiny is a small child, an infant
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Small lines are written beneath a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is foot soldiers collectively, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot as a military term means soldiers who fight on foot.

clue.text: Author gripped by violent urge, nevertheless

indicators.note: the name is held within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A writer is seized by a fierce desire all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian novelist, writer of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Shark may take plenty of interest in this

definitions.text: Shark may take plenty of interest in this

parts.words: Shark may take plenty of interest in this
parts.note: the shark is a usurer rather than a fish, and interest is the charge on money lent

explanation.surface: A predatory fish shows great curiosity about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' sounds like curiosity; it is the money charged by a loan shark, an illegal moneylender.
explanation.definitionFit: Money advanced to a borrower is what a usurer charges heavy interest on.

clue.text: Watch vital pump

definitions.meaning: slang for a timepiece that ticks
slang for the heart, the organ that keeps one alive

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the essential pump.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word both for a wristwatch and for the heart, both of which tick or beat.

clue.text: Like a member of the postmen's union?

definitions.text: Like a member of the postmen's union?

parts.words: Like a member of the postmen's union?
parts.note: a postman carries cards, and a full party member is said to carry a membership card

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of postal worker belongs to the union.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a fully paid-up member; postmen literally carry cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fully paid-up, committed party member holds a membership card, hence the phrase.

clue.text: One of the customers in an American restaurant

definitions.meaning: a person eating a meal at a restaurant
a cheap roadside eatery in the US

explanation.surface: A patron sits in a restaurant in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both someone eating out and a cheap US roadside eating place.

clue.text: Darling pet, Zola's coquette

definitions.meaning: the dog belonging to the Darling family in Peter Pan
the courtesan heroine of an Emile Zola novel

explanation.surface: A beloved animal is a flirt from a French novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' is the family name in Peter Pan, not an endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Darlings' dog nursemaid in Peter Pan and Zola's courtesan title heroine share the name.

clue.text: Master sculptor not initially seen as supreme creator

indicators.note: the opening letter of the sculptor's name is not seen, so it is removed

parts.note: Auguste Rodin was the great French sculptor of The Thinker

explanation.surface: A great sculptor at first goes unrecognised as the ultimate artist.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth the chief god shaped the world and humankind.

clue.text: I knew match might be rearranged for this London ground

indicators.note: the words are offered for rearrangement, so their letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone senses a fixture could be moved to a famous stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be rearranged' shuffles IKNEWMATCH; TWICKENHAM in south-west London is England's national rugby stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: This stadium in south-west London is the home of English rugby union.

clue.text: Sick, i.e. not well

explanation.surface: Feeling ill means not being in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses differ: an adjective meaning ill, and an adverb meaning badly done.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both ill in health and done badly or inadequately.

clue.text: Count rat going off as one?

definitions.text: Count rat going off as one?

indicators.note: something going off is breaking apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman deserts like a rat leaving a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' rearranges COUNTRAT; a rat, someone who deserts their side, is exactly what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat in slang is a traitor who changes sides, just like a defector.
